text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda include specification of goals in short-term economic policy.

- Duslo Sala, Slovakia's largest producer of artificial fertiliser, posted a pre-tax profit of 737 million crowns in the first half of this year, up from 274 million crowns in the same period last year. The company expect a slowdown in profit growth in the second half, saying pre-tax result for the full year should total about 400 million crowns.
- Slovakia's energy strategy says annual coal production should total 3.7 to 3.9 million tonnes in the next 10 years.
- Exports of the Slovak steel industry totalled 49.7 billion crowns in 1995, representing about 20 percent of the country's overall exports.

HOSPODARSKY NOVINY - The Finance Ministry will issue an unspecified tranche of one year state bonds on October 17. The coupon rate was set at 9.00 percent a year. The American-style auction will be held on October 15.
- Slovakia plans to invest 15 billion crowns in building the highways next year. Half of the sum will be invested by the state and the remaining part will be covered by bank loans.
- Parliament will discuss the new law on employment at the regular October session. The law should determine the active and passive employment policy and help invigorate the labour market.
- The price of milk and dairy products is expected to increase by about 20 percent at the beginning of next year.
- The Anti-Monopoly Bureau is not satisfied with the pace of development of small and medium-sized businesses and said more entrepreneurs were needed to increase the competition.
- Export-Import company Martimex has issued bonds totalling more than 200 million crowns to support the export production of the Slovak engineering industry.

SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Vladimir Valach, chairman of the supervisory board of Credit Lyonnais's Slovak branch, said the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has been showing a higher level of professionalism in managing the banking sector than its Czech counterpart.
- Valach said the NBS was strictly supervising the situation in the banks and its aim is to prevent the banks from having trouble with repayment of clients' deposits.
- Defence Minister Jan Sitek said foreign markets had shown serious interest in purchasing the Slovak-made howitzer Zuzana.
SME - The Transport Ministry said it would set the maximum and minimum tariffs for taxi companies.
